title: Majority: the count, the kings and the move
outcomes: Checks a majority against king distance and who is to move before trusting the count
Predicts a win, a draw or a king-first move in 3 against 2 endings
Says when the numbers on the wing do not matter

steps.text: You can now decide win or draw (see *Majority: win or draw, then which pawn*). The count is only one of three things. **Two more decide:** how near the enemy king is to the pawns, and **who is to move** (a tempo idea, as in *Opposition: one tempo between a win and a draw*). Look at one win, then at what changes.

steps.caption: White to move: three pawns against two on the kingside, the Black king far away on b7.

line.say: f4 offers an exchange. If Black takes, e3 recaptures and White has two pawns to Black's one.
White recaptures. The numbers on the wing are now two against one.

claims.statement: White has three pawns on the kingside.
Black has two pawns on the kingside.
After e4 the result for White is only a draw.
After the exchange White has two pawns on the kingside.
After the exchange Black has one pawn on the kingside.

steps.title: Same pawns, same kings, a tempo apart
steps.prompt: Three against two on the kingside. Predict the result in each position, then check.

steps.text: **Three cases in these positions.** Black king far from the pawns: White wins whoever moves. King in the middle distance: the side to move decides, a tempo question like the opposition. King close to the pawns: only a draw, even with White to move. **Rule of thumb:** count the majority first, then the kings, then the tempo; each can overrule the one before.

steps.prompt: Which of the three decided the positions you got wrong: the count, the king distance or the tempo?
